focus: Audit CLI session-continuity and lifecycle scenarios for Q2/Q3 fit, runner parity, missing compact/restart coverage, and value versus execution cost.

label: The existing Codex CX-017, OpenCode CO-018, Cursor CU-015 and Hermes HERMES-011 session-continuity scenarios all meet Q2 because each requires a second exchange that relies on prior state. Update style selectively: Codex and OpenCode can gain JSON conversation companions for interactive continuity, but retain their exact headless command checks; Cursor and Hermes stay manual until adapters exist because the runner accepts only Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi and Devin.

Update OpenCode CO-046 with a two-send JSON conversation: its current single prompt triggers a shell command, but the asserted `[session-relaunch]` marker must appear on a later captured request, so Q2 is yes. Keep the request-capture and event-file checks as evidence alongside the turn-by-turn runner checks; the current shell procedure also covers v1/v2 plugin paths.

Add a Pi-only JSON conversation companion to PI-020 for `/compact` followed by a state check or follow-up send. The current scenario explicitly skips `session_compact` in print mode and leaves `/compact` as an optional manual check; this is a Q2 gap because context must survive compaction, and the Pi adapter already exposes `/compact` plus per-turn checks.

The system-spec-kit Claude, Pi/OpenCode and command-runtime session-relaunch scenarios are Q2 candidates because task state crosses a process handoff, but keep their current wrapper and hook checks as the primary evidence. The shared runner's `restart` exits and resumes the same session ID through each adapter; it does not run `skilled-loop`, create or claim a handoff note, or prove Stop-hook arming. A JSON companion would add value only for the post-handoff operator exchange and must be labeled as partial coverage.

Rank PI-020 interactive compaction and CO-046 later-request capture first: both close an explicit uncovered Q2 behavior with one supported runtime and moderate authoring/run cost. Rank Codex/OpenCode continuity companions next, preserving exact CLI evidence; defer Cursor/Hermes conversion until adapters land. Keep system-spec-kit wrapper handoff scenarios manual until the runner can execute the wrapper lifecycle; replacing their shell evidence with same-session restart would give false coverage.
